data.narrative:
NuScale Power operates in the nuclear energy sector, a space with limited comparable public and private peers. The valuation universe comprises three publicly traded nuclear companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and five material private competitors including Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, Fuse Energy, and Terrestrial Energy. NuScale itself is public-stage with over $600M in cumulative capital raised.

Standard peer-median valuation methodology is not applicable here. The nuclear energy sector lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage peers meeting minimum sample thresholds—only one same-stage datapoint exists within the narrow peer set, falling short of the three-company minimum required for reliable median-based extrapolation. A broader all-sector median would introduce unacceptable sector-specific distortion and is therefore rejected as methodologically unsound.

Without a sufficiently dense peer set, this valuation requires alternative triangulation approaches: DCF analysis anchored to project-level cash flow assumptions, precedent transaction multiples (if available in the small-modular-reactor segment), or sum-of-the-parts methods applied to NuScale's portfolio of reactor designs and customer contracts. The extreme sparsity of same-tier comparables in nuclear energy represents the primary analytical constraint and suggests that valuation conclusions must rest heavily on company-specific unit economics and power-purchase agreement visibility rather than market-derived multiples.
